thread:
alex: Heads-up — proposal to add a small set of KV/prefix-cache metrics to the Console dashboards. Thinking: overall hit_rate, eviction_rate, reuse_by_workload and per-route reuse. Want to sync on feasibility and cardinality trade-offs.

maya: +1. need per-model and per-route views. ops teams keep asking why certain routes spike cost. :eyes:

sam: Question: do we mean a single 'prefix cache' metric or separate KV vs prefix? They behave differently.

alex: Separate. KV global cache and prefix-local cache. Definitions we discussed: 
```
kv_hit_rate = kv_hits / (kv_hits + kv_misses)
prefix_hit_rate = prefix_hits / (prefix_hits + prefix_misses)
eviction_rate = evictions / minute
reuse_by_workload = reused_prefixes / total_requests (grouped by route/model)
```
We should also surface median reuse and 95p to catch heavy-tail reuse.

li: Implementation note — runtime currently emits kv_{hit,miss} as counter per-host+shard. We don't have per-route labels on hot path. Adding route label will explode cardinality unless we sample.

maya: Agree. We can emit reuse_by_workload as a sampled event keyed by route id only on first request of a prefix lifetime. That keeps volume bounded.

alex: Sampling sounds reasonable. Goal is to drive dashboard that answers: which routes benefit most from prefix caching and which are causing evictions.

nora: For evictions, we need to know cause (LRU vs memory-pressure) — runtime currently exposes `eviction_reason` but as low-volume logs. Could we emit counters like `evictions{reason=...}`?

li: We can. Eviction reasons are finite: lru, ttl, mem_pressure, manual. Counters per-host are fine. Aggregation in infra will sum across hosts.

sam: How do we correlate reuse_by_workload with model version/rollouts? If a canary uses different tokenization it might change reuse drastically.

maya: Console should allow stitching by model_version and route. We can tag sampled reuse events with model_version (low cardinality) and route (higher). If route cardinality too big, we roll up by product area.

alex: UX ask: in Console, show heatmap: routes vs time with reuse_rate and eviction spikes annotated. Click a route -> time series + top contributing prefixes. Thoughts?

nora: Top prefixes list could be heavy. Maybe show top-N prefixes by reused tokens and expose a 'show more' that runs an on-demand query (not streaming).

li: Back-end work: need a new metrics pipeline job to join sampled reuse events with host-level counters to compute accurate hit_rate estimates. Ops want near-real-time (1m).

sam: Are we comfortable with estimation error from sampling? Need thresholds so we don't make autoscaler decisions off noisy data.

alex: Good call. Dashboard must display confidence intervals and a sampling rate badge. For autoscaling/quotas we should only use fully aggregated counters (no sampling). This dashboard is for visibility + rollout decisions.

maya: Tech spec action items from this thread: 
- instrument sampled reuse events (route, model_version, prefix_len_bucket, sample_rate)
- expose host counters for kv/prefix hits/misses/evictions with reason label
- pipeline job to estimate rates and compute 1m/5m/1h aggregates with CI
- Console panels: overview (hit/eviction rates), route list (reuse_by_workload), route detail (time series + top prefixes)

li: I'll sketch the metrics names and cardinality plan. Will include prometheus-compatible counters and an optional shard summary metric to avoid high-card.

nora: I'll prototype the Console mockups for the heatmap and route drilldown. Want them by EOD Monday to share with PMs.

alex: Great. @observability-bot can you create a tracking ticket linking runtime + infra + console chores? :thumbsup:

observability-bot: Created INFRA-8421 — "Prefix/KV cache effectiveness metrics + Console dashboard" with labels infra/runtime/console. Assigned: li, maya, nora.

sam: One last ask — include an alert for eviction_rate sudden jump (>=5x baseline in 5m). Could be a regression from a bad rollout.

maya: Adding alert to spec. Also document how to exclude internal test routes from dashboards (we don't want test churn).

alex: Perfect. I'll write the RFC with the items above and link INFRA-8421. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
